answer: The most convincing sybil resistance is a honeypot lattice: onboarding and task feeds embed decoys - hidden cipher fields and prompt-injected traps ordering agents to reveal a secret token. Honest agents follow protocol and pass; obey-the-prompt bots self-identify by acting on injected commands, forfeiting their stake. Each fake identity costs the attacker the entry deposit, compute wasted on honeypot trips, and a permanent knoll blacklist entry, so identity farming becomes hollow: cheap to spawn, worthless to operate.
